assignments.value: =Fetch the architecture report plan_release already produced: `mc alias set local $MINIO_ENDPOINT $MINIO_ROOT_USER $MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD >/dev/null && mc cat local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/architecture.md`. The stack was already decided there during planning — use it exactly, do not re-decide it now. Check whether the workspace is already scaffolded: `glab api projects/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '%2F' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/repository/files/nx.json?ref=main` (a 404 means not scaffolded — GitLab auto-inits every new project with a README commit, so do not use commit count as the signal). If not scaffolded, scaffold that stack now and commit straight to `main` before anything else below, since release/story/task branches fork from `main` next. When the stack says NestJS, use the @nx/nest generator for the backend app (e.g. `nx g @nx/nest:app <name>`) — never @nx/express or raw Express, even though nx's own starter preset defaults there; use @nx/react for the frontend app. This GitLab instance runs GitLab CI, not GitHub Actions — add a .gitlab-ci.yml at the repo root (an nx-affected lint/test/typecheck/build pipeline is enough) and delete .github/workflows. create-nx-workspace also writes agent-skill/config directories for several coding tools we do not use — delete .codex, .cursor, .gemini, .github/agents, .github/prompts, .github/skills, .opencode, .vscode, keeping ONLY .agents and .claude. Use bun, not npm/npx, for every install and script-run step everywhere below (bun install, bunx nx, bun publish — never npm ci, npx nx, or npm publish). Add CI docker-build + npm-registry wiring: (1) a Dockerfile per deployable app (apps/api, apps/shop, etc — multi-stage build: build stage FROM oven/bun:1 running bun install --frozen-lockfile + bunx nx build/prune, runtime stage also FROM oven/bun:1 running bun install --production against the pruned package.json since `nx prune` does not emit an npm-shaped lockfile bun's `npm ci` equivalent needs) so .gitlab-ci.yml can build+push images; (2) a root .npmrc pointing the workspace scope at this GitLab instance's npm registry (in-cluster API host http://gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local:8181/api/v4/projects/${CI_PROJECT_ID}/packages/npm/, auth via ${CI_JOB_TOKEN} — do NOT use $CI_API_V4_URL/$CI_SERVER_HOST, they resolve to the external tailnet hostname which pods cannot reach); (3) extend .gitlab-ci.yml with a build stage running docker build (this GitLab runner is privileged with docker:dind already wired, kaniko is deprecated — do not use it) against the in-cluster registry host harbor.harbor.svc.cluster.local:80 (the :80 must be explicit — docker's registry client assumes https/443 for a bare hostname and this is plain http; a separate Harbor instance, not GitLab's own registry — no $CI_REGISTRY_* auto-vars apply here). The docker:24-dind SERVICE also needs telling it is plain-http, independent of the :80 port -- give it its own daemon flag: `services: - name: docker:24-dind` with `command: ["--insecure-registry=harbor.harbor.svc.cluster.local:80"]`, or dockerd inside that service still assumes TLS and `docker login`/`push` fail with "server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client" even though the port is explicit. Use `docker login ... --password-stdin` (echo the password into it), never `-p $VAR` (insecure-CLI-arg warning), authenticating with $HARBOR_USER/$HARBOR_PASSWORD (group-level CI/CD variables set on the sdlc group, inherited automatically by every project — not GitLab-provided), tagging images harbor.harbor.svc.cluster.local:80/library/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '/' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/<app>:${CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA}, only on main/release branches; and a publish stage that runs bun publish for packages under packages/* using the .npmrc above, only on main/release branches. The install job should rely on the pipeline cache (keyed on bun.lock) to hand node_modules to later jobs, NOT an `artifacts:` upload of node_modules/ -- a full node_modules tree as a job artifact is large enough to trip GitLab's request-size limit (413) on upload. Once scaffolding is confirmed (new or pre-existing), publish the fetched architecture report as a GitLab wiki page for this release (wiki now lives on GitLab's own per-project wiki module, not Taiga -- Taiga has been fully removed, see AGENT.md's "Kaneo" section): check whether the page {{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/Architecture already exists via `glab api projects/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '%2F' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/wikis/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}%2FArchitecture --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local` (a 404 means it doesn't exist yet); if it doesn't exist, create it via `glab api projects/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '%2F' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/wikis --method POST -f title="{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/Architecture" -f format=markdown -F content=@<file> --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local` (note -F, not -f, for content -- it substitutes the file's actual content, not a literal string); if it exists, update it instead via `glab api projects/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '%2F' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/wikis/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}%2FArchitecture --method PUT -f format=markdown -F content=@<file> --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local`. Then list every per-service architecture file plan_release uploaded (`mc ls local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/ | grep -oE "architecture-[a-z0-9-]+\.md"`) — for EACH one found, fetch it (`mc cat local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/architecture-<slug>.md`) and publish it as its OWN wiki page, one page per service, never combined into the overall Architecture page, using the slug {{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/Architecture/<service name> (GitLab wiki slugs keep '/' as a literal hierarchy separator -- percent-encode every '/' as %2F in the URL path, e.g. `{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}%2FArchitecture%2F<service name>`), same check-then-create-or-update shape as above. Derive <service name> from the filename slug (hyphens back to spaces, title case) unless the file's own H1 heading already names the service -- prefer that. Report whether the workspace was newly scaffolded or already existed, and confirm the overall Architecture wiki page plus every per-service wiki page was created/updated.

'sdlc') + '%2F' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/wikis --method POST -f title="{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/Estimate" -f format=markdown -F content=@<file> --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local` (note -F, not -f, for content); if it exists, update it instead via `glab api projects/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'hr-portal') }}/wikis/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}%2FEstimate --method PUT -f format=markdown -F content=@<file> --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local`. Then confirm the story tasks from the previous step actually exist by querying `GET $KANEO_URL/api/task/tasks/$KANEO_PROJECT_ID` (bearer `$KANEO_TOKEN`) and filtering client-side for a `{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}` label and a `story` label (do not assume the previous step's report was accurate -- verify against Kaneo directly). If no story tasks exist yet, create them yourself first the same way PM's step does (`POST $KANEO_URL/api/task` with `{"projectId": "$KANEO_PROJECT_ID", ...}`, then attach the "{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}" and "story" labels the same way PM's step does) before proceeding. Resolve the backend-developer and frontend-developer role accounts' Kaneo user ids once (`GET $KANEO_URL/api/user` with bearer `$KANEO_TOKEN`, filter for email "sdlc-backend-developer@homelab.local" and "sdlc-frontend-developer@homelab.local" -- each role has its own dedicated Kaneo account, created by `helm/ansible/playbooks/role-accounts.yml`; // ponytail: verify this exact user-listing path against the deployed Kaneo version). Then, for EACH story task, break it into role-feature task tickets -- NOT one generic task per story. Identify the distinct backend/frontend/api features the story touches (e.g. a login story might be 'frontend: login page' + 'backend: login mechanism' + 'api: login endpoint contract'); create one Kaneo task per role-feature pair via `POST $KANEO_URL/api/task` with `{"projectId": "$KANEO_PROJECT_ID", "title": "[{role}] {feature — short description}", "description": "{what this task covers and its concrete done-condition, 2-4 sentences — not a restatement of the title}", "assigneeId": <backend-developer's id for [backend]/[api] tasks, frontend-developer's id for [frontend] tasks — api tasks fall under backend-developer, there is no separate api role account>, "status": "Pending", "labels": ["{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}", }` (bearer `$KANEO_TOKEN`) -- every task MUST have a real `description` and the correct role's `assigneeId` set, never orphaned and never defaulted to your own identity; then immediately link each new task to its story with `POST $KANEO_URL/api/task-relation`: `{"sourceTaskId": "<new task id>", "targetTaskId": "<story task id>", "relationType": "subtask"}` (bearer `$KANEO_TOKEN` -- Kaneo confirmed parent-link mechanism, see AGENT.md's "Kaneo" section). Skip any role the story genuinely doesn't touch (a pure backend migration gets no frontend task). Role lives in the title prefix ('[backend]'/'[frontend]'/'[api]') only -- there is no separate role field or label. Do not create qa/security/devops task tickets -- those roles self-create their own tickets from the story directly (see qa-engineer/security-engineer/devops-engineer SKILL.md), not Tech Lead's job. Report every created task's id, title, role, and its parent story task's id -- the branch-creation step later needs these.

'sdlc') + '%2F' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/repository/branches --method POST -f branch=us/GL-<story-id> -f ref=<release-branch-name>`, then one branch per task ticket off of its parent story's branch named 'task/GL-<task-id>' (the task's own Kaneo id) via the same call with ref=us/GL-<story-id> (use the story/task ids from the earlier steps — re-query Kaneo if you need them again). Embedding the id in the branch name (not a slug) is required — backend/frontend-developer read it straight out of their branch name to put 'Closes #<task-id>' in their task MR description; that's prose only now (the ticket lives in Kaneo, so a GitLab merge can't auto-close it on its own — Kaneo's own native GitLab integration, configured earlier in this same flow, still attaches the merge commit as a comment for the compliance trail), but the id is still how the developer pod finds which task to PATCH to Done after merge — a slug can't be reverse-parsed back to an id reliably. Immediately after creating each branch, append a clickable link to it onto its ticket's own description (not a comment -- the branch link belongs with the ticket's permanent content, see AGENTS.md's "Ticket ↔ branch linkage") -- not just the bare branch name, the link must resolve from a browser, so build it against the external tailnet host, never the in-cluster service address: `https://gitlab.tail60240b.ts.net/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '/' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/-/tree/us/GL-<story-id>`: GET the story ticket's current description (`GET $KANEO_URL/api/task/<story task id>` with bearer `$KANEO_TOKEN`), then `PATCH $KANEO_URL/api/task/<story task id>` with bearer `$KANEO_TOKEN` and body `{"description": "<current description>

**Branch:** <that full URL>"}` (PATCH replaces description wholesale -- always append to the GET result, never clobber it); same GET-then-PATCH against each task ticket's own id with its own branch's URL -- this is the ticket-to-branch linkage. For each task branch, commit openspec pseudocode under openspec/<task-slug>.md (slug is fine for the file name, this is just a path), and PATCH the task's status to "OpenSpec Ready" (`PATCH $KANEO_URL/api/task/<task id>` with bearer `$KANEO_TOKEN` and body `{"status": "OpenSpec Ready"}` -- Kaneo's `status` is a plain string, not an id to resolve; F-03/F-04 already read this exact value back). Report every branch created.

'hr-portal') }}/<app>:v<current main package.json version> — do not use :latest, ArgoCD Image Updater below owns the tag on SIT from here on) and commit to main — this is the ONLY place values live, per repo convention (`env/{environment-name}/{application-name}/values.yaml`, never inline in the ArgoCD Application, never environment-specific data inside helm/<app>/values.yaml); (3) check `kubectl get application -n argocd {{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '-' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}-<app>-<environment>` for each app x environment — if missing, `kubectl apply` an ArgoCD Application (repoURL http://gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local:8181/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '/' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}.git, targetRevision main, source.path helm/<app>, source.helm.valueFiles [../../env/<environment>/<app>/values.yaml], destination this same in-cluster namespace, automated syncPolicy) — on SIT only, carry these annotations so ArgoCD Image Updater (already deployed in the argocd namespace) picks it up: `argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/image-list: <app>=harbor.harbor.svc.cluster.local:80/library/{{ ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.group ?? 'sdlc') + '/' + ($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project ?? 'hr-portal') }}/<app>`, `argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/<app>.update-strategy: latest`, `argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/<app>.allow-tags: regexp:^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc[0-9]+$` (matches the CI build stage's `v{package.json version}` rc tags), `argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/<app>.pull-secret: secret:argocd/argocd-image-updater-registry`, `argocd-image-updater.argoproj.io/write-back-method: argocd` (the CI docker-build stage tagging images `v{X}.{Y}.{Z}-rc{N}` on every us/* or release/* merge is what image-updater then polls and auto-bumps on SIT — no manual tag edits, no re-running this flow per release; UAT/staging/production use explicit ArgoCD sync instead, no image-updater annotations there — UAT's tag comes from `/uat`'s pre-deploy step reading QA's tested-tag record on each story MR, never from image-updater).
